steps.message: Unit tests can't run (test-only dependencies aren't in the offline cache / network blocked), but `assembleDebug` compiles cleanly. Here's the final patch:

## Diagnosis

**Location:** `AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/dialogs/CustomStudyDialog.java`, in `createCustomStudySession()`.

**Cause:** When a *non-dynamic* deck already exists with the name "Custom study session", the code tried to warn the user by building and showing a brand new `MaterialDialog` from inside the `onPositive` callback of the `CustomStudyDialog` `DialogFragment`:

```java
new MaterialDialog.Builder(getActivity())
    .content(R.string.custom_study_deck_exists)
    .negativeText(R.string.dialog_cancel)
    .build().show();
```

That dialog is a plain, activity-owned dialog created while the fragment's own dialog is being dismissed and the custom-study menu stack unwinds (the OK click dismisses the input dialog and returns to/closes the previous menu). The teardown window torn down / covered the freshly-shown warning dialog, so the user only saw the UI "go back one menu item" and never read the "Rename the existing custom study deck first" message.

**Fix:** Replace the transient, lifecycle-fragile dialog with a themed toast — exactly the "ideal solution" in the report, and consistent with the neighbouring error path in the same method (`custom_study_rebuild_deck_corrupt`):

```java
UIUtils.showThemedToast(this.getContext(), getString(R.string.custom_study_deck_exists), true);
```

A toast is not tied to the dialog/fragment window, so it remains visible after the custom-study dialogs dismiss. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: the method still returns early without creating/overwriting the user's existing deck. `MaterialDialog`/`UIUtils` imports were already present and still used, and `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` succeeds.
